newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares rise in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares rise in Beirut.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares rose on Tuesday on the Beirut Secondary Market (BSM), continuing a rally begun last week attributed by dealers to expectations that the company plans to launch a $150 million GDR issue.
A shares rose two percent on the privately-operated BSM to $114.625 from Monday's $112.375 and B shares rose 2.3 percent to $116.375 from $113.750.

Dealers say momentum is building up on the Beirut equities market because of expectations that SOLIDERE, which is in charge of rebuilding the war-damaged Beirut centre, will launch a $150 million Global Depositary Receipts issue in mid-October, giving non-Arab investors access to the market for the first time.
SOLIDERE declined to comment on the report which followed rumours on the Beirut market.
Turnover on the BSM, which trades only SOLIDERE shares, rose to 20,036 shares from Monday's 12,724 shares and value was $2,296,841 from $1,414,412.875.
No shares were traded on the Beirut Stock Exchange in any of the four listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs SCBB BY, Eternit ETR.BY and Uniceramic UNIB.BY.
On Monday, Ciments Libanais SCL.BY was steady at $1.375 on sale of 200 shares and Eternit ETR. BY was also steady at $1.9375 with 1,000 shares sold.
The LISPI index which covers both markets rose 0.61 percent to 85.47.
